display.title: Episode 133: The Two Brothers (Shiva Asar B'Tammuz)
display.summary_short: On the fast of the 17th of Tammuz, a show without music: why Hashem chose Har HaMoriah for the Beis HaMikdash, a letter from a boy's Yetzer Tov, and what happened on this day long ago.
display.summary_long: Broadcast on Shiva Asar B'Tammuz, the first day of the Three Weeks, with no music. Uncle Yossi explains that only Torah and mitzvos unite the Jewish people, and that Hashem's blessing comes when we are 'all as one', as we say in davening. After a young guest who carries the Twelve Pesukim booklet everywhere leads the Shema, he tells the story of two brothers in Yerushalayim. Reuven, with many children, and Shimon, with none, each secretly carries wheat at night to the other's barn, until they meet at the top of the mountain, drop their loads and embrace. Hashem chose that mountain, Har HaMoriah, for His Beis HaMikdash, because the Shechinah rests where there is love. The Beis HaMikdash was destroyed through baseless hatred and will be rebuilt through Ahavas Yisroel. The mailbox brings an eight-year-old's letter in Yiddish, written by his Yetzer Tov to his Yetzer Hara, boasting how he davens, learns and makes brachos even better when told not to. Finally Uncle Yossi traces the events of the 17th of Tammuz under Nevuchadnetzar, when the daily korban stopped, and looks forward to the day these fasts become Yamim Tovim.
display.lesson: The Beis HaMikdash was destroyed through baseless hatred and will be rebuilt through Ahavas Yisroel; Hashem rests His Presence where Jews love one another.
